fields.title: Search moat ruled in court as 'metamorphosis' not 'erosion'
fields.html:
1. What happened

On September 2, 2026, a U.S. court rejected Google's ad-tech business divestiture order. The court decided not to adopt the remedies proposed by the DOJ to separate the ad auction platforms (DV360·Google Ads Manager). This means Google can maintain the core infrastructure of its search advertising business intact. At the same time, the court specified only limited remedies for Google's advertising publisher platforms (AdSense·Ad Manager) business.

2. Connection to the 10-year thesis

This becomes the best verification opportunity for Core Hypothesis 1 of the thesis director: 'The search moat is in metamorphosis, not erosion.' Had the court completely separated the ad network, the value chain of search advertising would have been substantially weakened in automated bidding and targeting capabilities. In that case, 'search death' would have become voluntary stranding by regulation.

However, the ruling outcome is the opposite. The court's decision can be interpreted as recognizing 'search + ad network integration' as an 'efficiency factor' rather than 'antitrust harm.' This suggests external (court) recognition of the thesis's premise that the search moat lies in technical and structural superiority rather than mere market share. Moreover, it supports the possibility that the 'conclusion Buffett reached ($36.6 billion three-tranche acquisition)' documented in the thesis was reading a signal of regulatory loosening rather than regulatory risk avoidance.

3. Thesis assessment

[Reinforced] Legal recognition that search moat is not structurally eroded even by regulatory divestiture. The second basis of capex fear (search advertising durability) has been downgraded one level from policy risk.

4. What could be wrong

The court judgment has not been finalized, and DOJ appeal or other pending litigation remains possible. Additionally, a ruling of 'no divestiture' may come with behavioral remedies like 'improvements to ad platform terms of service,' which could gradually erode ad-tech profitability in the long term. It is difficult to interpret as a clean victory without reading the actual conditional clauses in the judgment text. Moreover, this ruling reflects the DOJ policy shift under a Republican administration (moderation in antitrust litigation), so the possibility of renewed litigation remains if political circumstances change.

5. Next observation points

  • 3Q earnings release (end of October 2026): Verify whether search advertising growth rate maintains double-digit levels. Test whether regulatory relief translates to actual revenue stability.
  • DOJ appeal notification (September–October 2026): Monitor the degree of ongoing legal uncertainty until final judgment confirmation.
  • Detailed disclosure of ad-tech remedies: After the court's 'limited remedies' are publicly disclosed as specific terms-of-service and technology constraints, reassess profitability impact.
